**Likely yes, but the loss is not yet corroborated under the tool’s rule.** Satellite data detected 13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the property. Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classified 13.1 hectares of that area as native forest, and the JRC mapped 98% of the event area as forest in 2020.

The corroboration rule also requires an observation from a later year. None is available yet, so the detected loss remains uncorroborated.
